Chapter 10: Choosing Glory Over Extinction
At some point, we all face those big, unavoidable questions. What sort of ancestors do we want to be remembered as? What kind of legacy are we really leaving for the people who’ll come after us?
Here’s the thing: choosing between extinction and glory isn’t about one, dramatic moment. It’s actually a bunch of small choices, day in and day out.
Picture this—the story draws to a close with a young person, standing at the edge of a quiet forest, gazing out over a world that’s both stunning and fragile. The future? It’s uncertain, sure... but it’s wide open with possibility.
Most of us aren’t going to be famous, or hold huge amounts of power. But every single one of us can decide to act with integrity, to show compassion, and to find courage—even when it’s hard.
Imagine a family gathered around the dinner table, swapping stories about their struggles and their hopes. The conversation drifts toward what’s next, and for just a moment, you can feel it—this powerful sense that the future is still ours to shape.
And that’s the heart of it: real glory isn’t about being celebrated or conquering anything. It’s about living in a way that honors what’s best in us as human beings.
The truth is, this choice isn’t always easy. The risks? They’re very real. But drifting toward extinction—just because we’re afraid or apathetic? That’s not an option anyone wants.
Our future will be built by those willing to imagine something better—and who keep working toward it, one day at a time.
